input.quote: 10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement has no limitation of liability, exclusion of damages or aggregate-liability language anywhere: searches for "liability", "damages", "consequential", "indemnif" and "aggregate" return only the no-joint-venture provision (10.2) and the Termination Payment calculation (4.2), and the Warranties (Section 9) and General Provisions (Section 10) articles contain no cap. Because the rule expects a cap and none exists, this is a missing clause rather than a deviation. We inserted a new Section 10.9 (within the surviving Section 10) reflecting the preferred position: a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable by the Company and USD 1,000,000, mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmation that the Company's payment obligations (Sections 3 and 4.2) are not "damages". Note the fee basis is meaningful here (30% of Net Sales under Section 3.1), so a fee-based cap is not illusory; the fallback of a straight twelve-month fee cap is offered in the comment.

ops.text: 10.9 Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000), and neither Party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. The Company's obligations to make payments under Sections 3 and 4.2 are not "damages" and are not subject to the foregoing limitation.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no limitation of liability, so both parties are exposed to unlimited and consequential damages; we have added our standard mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees or USD 1,000,000, with confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sitting outside the cap. If helpful, we can accept a straight twelve-month fee cap with carve-outs for indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
proposal.summary: Add mutual limitation of liability with 12-month fee/USD 1M cap and standard uncapped carve-outs
